papers.title: Risk Factors of Failure to Discharge Before “Two Midnights” in Outpatient-Designated Total Hip Arthroplasty
papers.abstract: INTRODUCTION: The Centers for Medicare and Medicaid Services removed total hip arthroplasty (THA) from the inpatient-only list but continued to classify admissions as inpatient if they include two midnights, complicating care if an outpatient THA requires extended hospitalization. This study evaluates risk factors of patients undergoing outpatient-designated THA with a length of stay (LOS) ≥ 2 days. METHODS: A total of 17,063 THA procedures designated as outpatient in the National Surgical Quality Improvement Program database between 2015 and 2020 were stratified by LOS < 2 days (n = 2,294, 13.4%) and LOS ≥ 2 days (n = 14,765, 86.6%). Demographics, comorbidities, and outcomes were compared by univariate analysis. Multivariable regression analysis identified predictors of LOS ≥ 2 days. RESULTS: Outpatients with extended LOS were older (mean 65.3 vs. 63.5 years; P < 0.01); were more likely to have body mass index (BMI) > 35 (24.0 vs. 17.8%; P < 0.01); and had higher incidences of smoking (15.1% vs. 10.3%; P < 0.01), diabetes (15.4% vs. 9.9%; P < 0.01), chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (4.4% vs. 2.3%; P < 0.01), and hypertension (57.6% vs. 49.2%; P < 0.01). Patients with LOS ≥ 2 days had a higher incidence of surgical site infection ( P < 0.01), hospital readmission ( P < 0.01), and revision surgery ( P < 0.01) over 30 days. Multivariable analysis demonstrated advanced age, female sex, African American race, Hispanic ethnicity, diabetes, smoking, and hypertension were independent risk factors for LOS ≥ 2 days. CONCLUSION: Despite removal from the inpatient-only list, a subset of outpatient THA remains at risk of an extended LOS. This study informs surgeons on the relevant risk factors of extended stay, enabling early inpatient preauthorization.

papers.title: Enhanced recovery after surgery: Singapore General Hospital arthroplasty experience
papers.abstract: INTRODUCTION Total knee arthroplasty (TKA) and total hip arthroplasty (THA) are effective treatments for end-stage osteoarthritis of the knee and hip, with increasing demand for these surgeries being projected to rise substantially along with the cost to the healthcare system.[1] In the past, a week-long hospitalisation after TKA was the norm as there had been concerns that reduction in length of stay (LOS) would correspond with increase in postoperative complications.[2] Enhanced recovery after surgery (ERAS) or fast-track surgery has evolved over the decades and has been proven effective across a range of procedures to reduce the LOS and morbidity, without an increase in readmission rates or safety issues.[3,4] Its applicability for postoperative care and recovery for patients undergoing major orthopaedic arthroplasty procedures (THA and TKA) has also grown over the years.[5] The drive to implement ERAS protocols and day surgery arthroplasties has particularly grown during the coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19) pandemic to ensure business continuity in the setting of shortage of hospital beds and resources globally[6,7] and locally.[8] DISCUSSION The proponents of ERAS believe that perioperative care is equally important as TKA and THA procedures in dictating patient outcomes, and detailed guidelines have been recommended by the ERAS Society to help guide surgical centres in this transition.[9] The ERAS protocols were implemented with the aim to reduce average LOS for patients undergoing TKA with less than 5 days inpatient stay. Some studies in the literature[10,11] show that the mean LOS in ERAS TKA has safely shortened from 4–5 days to 3 days. In 2019, Singapore General Hospital (SGH) launched the ERAS pathway for patients undergoing TKA and started to offer TKA as a day surgery procedure in August 2020 during the height of the COVID-19 pandemic, whereby majority of the healthcare resources were diverted towards the fight of the pandemic.[12,13,14] This was to allow continuation of musculoskeletal care and elective procedures, such as TKA, to reduce utilisation of inpatient hospital bed as well as minimise potential patient COVID-19 exposure in the hospital setting after surgery. The ERAS day surgery TKA protocol refers to expedited discharge either on the day of surgery or on postoperative day (POD) 1, with patients being discharged within 23 h after surgery. These patients were considered to have successfully cleared the ERAS TKA protocol after they were cleared by the primary surgeon and the physiotherapist. Recommendations from the ERAS Society consensus statement were implemented in line with hospital guidelines. Preoperatively, patients received counselling on their surgery and the expected recovery progress by both the primary surgeon and the physiotherapist. Patients were evaluated by an anaesthetist, and smoking cessation advice was given as required. Preoperative anaemia screening was performed and patients were started on iron supplementation if indicated. All patients underwent physiotherapy review before operation and received prehabilitation. Perioperatively, patients were fasted for at least 6 h before the operation, with clear fluids allowed until 2 h before induction. A carbohydrate drink consisting of 50 g of glucose was given 2 h before surgery with oral preemptive analgesia (etoricoxib 120 mg and omeprazole 20 mg if no contraindications) (body mass index [BMI] >35 kg/m2, history of gastrointestinal reflux, diabetes mellitus). Intraoperatively, all cases were planned for spinal anaesthesia unless contraindicated (e.g. previous spinal instrumentation). No femoral nerve block was given. Intravenous (IV) cefazolin was given at the start of surgery and IV clindamycin was given for patients with penicillin allergy. The use of tourniquet was left to the preference of the individual surgeons. For postoperative nausea and vomiting prophylaxis, all patients received IV dexamethasone 8 mg at the start of surgery and IV ondansetron 8 mg at the end of surgery. All patients received a periarticular infiltration of ketorolac, shincort, vancomycin and morphine, as well as an adductor canal block given intraoperatively by the surgeon. Topical tranexamic acid was applied before knee capsular closure. Postoperatively, patient-controlled analgesia (e.g., morphine) and epidurals were not used. Patients were given a combination of oral analgesia (paracetamol, etoricoxib, pregabalin and tramadol) for pain control. Oral aspirin was started on POD 1 for 1–2 weeks, and patients underwent physiotherapy for ambulation on the same day after surgery. In addition, the protocol at SGH comprises home visit by a physiotherapist at the first week after surgery and home visit by a nurse at the second week after surgery. There was a steady increase in the proportion of ERAS TKA between 2020 and 2021, with more than 20% of TKAs performed as ERAS for 2021. During the period from August 2020 to July 2021, there were 738 patients who underwent unilateral TKA at SGH, with 342 ERAS day surgeries (aiming for discharge within 23 h) and 396 conventional TKAs (discharge after 23 h). The inclusion criteria were (a) American Society of Anesthesiologists (ASA) ≤3 and (b) patient who agreed to be discharged home. Patients who declined discharge within 23 h were enrolled for conventional TKA. There were 92.4% of patients in the ERAS day surgery group, who were successfully discharged home within 23 h, leading to a significant shorter mean LOS of 1.13 (±1.0) days compared to 4.12 (±3.3) days in the conventional group (P < 0.005). Some of the common reasons for patients failing ERAS day surgery TKA protocol and getting discharged after 23 h included decision to transfer to step-down facility (community hospital), postoperative nausea and vomiting, acute urinary retention and inadequate pain control. Patients who underwent ERAS day surgery compared to conventional TKA inpatient group had significantly better preoperative patient-reported outcome measure scores (PROMs) in terms of knee society scores, Oxford knee scores and Short Form-36 scores (P < 0.05). Both groups had postoperative improvement of PROMs well above the minimal clinically important difference at 6 months follow-up. There was no increase in the rates of 30-day readmission and complications (readmission rate 2.6% in ERAS day surgery vs. 2.5% in conventional group, P = 0.928; infection 1.5% vs. 0.8%, P = 0.357; reoperation 0.9% vs. 0.5%, P = 0.130). There were no significant associations between age, gender, Charlson comorbidity index, ASA classification, BMI and the successful completion of ERAS day surgery TKA as compared to those who did not manage to be discharged within 23 h. There were also no differences in PROMs for patients who did not manage to be discharged within 23 h compared to that of those who underwent ERAS day surgery TKA at 6 months follow-up. These results are promising in terms of promoting ERAS day surgery TKA as a safe standard of care model for patients to be discharged in an expedited and timely manner with no compromise in patient outcomes and complication rates, and also to encourage inclusion of more patients into this pathway, especially in view of the rapidly ageing population in Singapore. It is also more cost-efficient for both the patients and health care as the median cost of ERAS TKA is significantly lower than that of non-ERAS TKA cases. This is largely due to the savings in hospital room charges, daily treatment fees and services due to the shorter LOS for ERAS TKA patients. In SGH, before ERAS TKA, day surgery THA was performed through the direct anterior approach, with up to 82% of patients being discharged within the same day of surgery with satisfactory results postoperatively and no major complications observed.[15] Subsequently, posterior approach day surgery THA was offered to patients at SGH. There are approximately 100 cases of ERAS posterior approach THA. We are still working on preliminary data analysis, and future studies will report on the clinical outcomes of all ERAS THA, including our results between the traditional posterior approach and the direct anterior approach THA, which is gaining popularity in many orthopaedic surgery centres.[16] We anticipate that there will be increasing number of patients who will be able to benefit from the ERAS protocol for total joint arthroplasties (TKA and THA) to safely reduce the length of inpatient stay without compromising on clinical outcomes and complication rates. TAKE HOME MESSAGES Successful ERAS protocols involve a multidisciplinary approach for patient care. ERAS protocols can be safely implemented for day surgery total join arthroplasty. The THA and TKA patients can safely have shorter LOS without compromising on outcomes and with no increased risk of complications. With increasing number of patients undergoing ERAS inpatient and day surgery total joint arthroplasty, more concrete findings and reports can be published in the upcoming years. Financial support and sponsorship Nil. Conflicts of interest There are no conflicts of interest.

papers.title: How Inverse Conditional Flows Can Serve as a Substitute for Distributional Regression
papers.abstract: Neural network representations of simple models, such as linear regression, are being studied increasingly to better understand the underlying principles of deep learning algorithms. However, neural representations of distributional regression models, such as the Cox model, have received little attention so far. We close this gap by proposing a framework for distributional regression using inverse flow transformations (DRIFT), which includes neural representations of the aforementioned models. We empirically demonstrate that the neural representations of models in DRIFT can serve as a substitute for their classical statistical counterparts in several applications involving continuous, ordered, time-series, and survival outcomes. We confirm that models in DRIFT empirically match the performance of several statistical methods in terms of estimation of partial effects, prediction, and aleatoric uncertainty quantification. DRIFT covers both interpretable statistical models and flexible neural networks opening up new avenues in both statistical modeling and deep learning.

papers.title: Controlling Chaos Using Edge Computing Hardware
papers.abstract: Machine learning provides a data-driven approach for creating a digital twin of a system - a digital model used to predict the system behavior. Having an accurate digital twin can drive many applications, such as controlling autonomous systems. Often the size, weight, and power consumption of the digital twin or related controller must be minimized, ideally realized on embedded computing hardware that can operate without a cloud-computing connection. Here, we show that a nonlinear controller based on next-generation reservoir computing can tackle a difficult control problem: controlling a chaotic system to an arbitrary time-dependent state. The model is accurate, yet it is small enough to be evaluated on a field-programmable gate array typically found in embedded devices. Furthermore, the model only requires 25.0 $\pm$ 7.0 nJ per evaluation, well below other algorithms, even without systematic power optimization. Our work represents the first step in deploying efficient machine learning algorithms to the computing "edge."

papers.title: Latent Variable Double Gaussian Process Model for Decoding Complex Neural Data
papers.abstract: Non-parametric models, such as Gaussian Processes (GP), show promising results in the analysis of complex data. Their applications in neuroscience data have recently gained traction. In this research, we introduce a novel neural decoder model built upon GP models. The core idea is that two GPs generate neural data and their associated labels using a set of low-dimensional latent variables. Under this modeling assumption, the latent variables represent the underlying manifold or essential features present in the neural data. When GPs are trained, the latent variable can be inferred from neural data to decode the labels with a high accuracy. We demonstrate an application of this decoder model in a verbal memory experiment dataset and show that the decoder accuracy in predicting stimulus significantly surpasses the state-of-the-art decoder models. The preceding performance of this model highlights the importance of utilizing non-parametric models in the analysis of neuroscience data.

summary_en.motivation: To leverage non-parametric models for decoding complex neural data with high accuracy.
summary_en.method: A latent variable double Gaussian process model is proposed to jointly generate neural data and labels from low-dimensional latent variables.
summary_en.result: The decoder achieves superior accuracy in predicting stimulus in a verbal memory experiment compared to state-of-the-art models.
summary_en.validation: Validation is performed on a real neural dataset from a verbal memory experiment.

papers.title: ASPIRE: Iterative Amortized Posterior Inference for Bayesian Inverse Problems
papers.abstract: Due to their uncertainty quantification, Bayesian solutions to inverse problems are the framework of choice in applications that are risk averse. These benefits come at the cost of computations that are in general, intractable. New advances in machine learning and variational inference (VI) have lowered the computational barrier by learning from examples. Two VI paradigms have emerged that represent different tradeoffs: amortized and non-amortized. Amortized VI can produce fast results but due to generalizing to many observed datasets it produces suboptimal inference results. Non-amortized VI is slower at inference but finds better posterior approximations since it is specialized towards a single observed dataset. Current amortized VI techniques run into a sub-optimality wall that can not be improved without more expressive neural networks or extra training data. We present a solution that enables iterative improvement of amortized posteriors that uses the same networks architectures and training data. The benefits of our method requires extra computations but these remain frugal since they are based on physics-hybrid methods and summary statistics. Importantly, these computations remain mostly offline thus our method maintains cheap and reusable online evaluation while bridging the approximation gap these two paradigms. We denote our proposed method ASPIRE - Amortized posteriors with Summaries that are Physics-based and Iteratively REfined. We first validate our method on a stylized problem with a known posterior then demonstrate its practical use on a high-dimensional and nonlinear transcranial medical imaging problem with ultrasound. Compared with the baseline and previous methods from the literature our method stands out as an computationally efficient and high-fidelity method for posterior inference.

llm.relevance_to_user: 该论文提出的迭代式摊销变分推断方法可显著提升贝叶斯逆问题的计算效率与不确定性量化精度，有望迁移至植入物力学设计的代理模型与优化中。
llm.why_not_core: This paper does not apply the method to FEA surrogate modeling or implant biomechanics; it validates on a medical imaging problem instead.

summary_zh.motivation: 现有摊销变分推断在贝叶斯逆问题中精度受限，需迭代改进。
summary_zh.method: 提出ASPIRE方法，利用物理混合摘要统计量迭代优化摊销后验。
summary_zh.result: 在保持在线高效的同时，显著缩小了与专用推断的精度差距。
summary_zh.validation: 在已知后验的简化问题和高维超声成像问题上验证。

summary_en.motivation: Amortized variational inference for Bayesian inverse problems suffers from suboptimal posterior approximations that cannot be improved without more expressive networks or more data.
summary_en.method: ASPIRE iteratively refines amortized posteriors using physics-hybrid summary statistics, keeping most computations offline to maintain cheap online evaluation.
summary_en.result: The method bridges the approximation gap between amortized and non-amortized VI, achieving high-fidelity posterior inference with computational efficiency.
summary_en.validation: Validation on a stylized problem with known posterior and a high-dimensional nonlinear transcranial ultrasound imaging problem.

papers.title: Coupling of the Finite Element Method with Physics Informed Neural Networks for the Multi-Fluid Flow Problem
papers.abstract: Multi-fluid flows are found in various industrial processes, including metal injection molding and 3D printing. The accuracy of multi-fluid flow modeling is determined by how well interfaces and capillary forces are represented. In this paper, the multi-fluid flow problem is discretized using a combination of a Physics-Informed Neural Network (PINN) with a finite element discretization. To determine the best PINN formulation, a comparative study is conducted using a manufactured solution. We compare interface reinitialization methods to determine the most suitable approach for our discretization strategy. We devise a neural network architecture that better handles complex free surface topologies. Finally, the coupled numerical strategy is used to model a rising bubble problem.

llm.why_not_core: This paper focuses on multi-fluid flow problems (e.g., bubble rising) rather than solid mechanics or implant biomechanics, and lacks uncertainty quantification, constraint handling, or transferability to implant design.

summary_en.motivation: To improve the accuracy of interface and capillary force representation in multi-fluid flow simulations.
summary_en.method: A coupled approach combining Physics-Informed Neural Networks with finite element discretization, with a comparative study of interface reinitialization methods.
summary_en.result: The proposed numerical strategy successfully models a rising bubble problem.
summary_en.validation: Validation via manufactured solution and a rising bubble simulation case.

papers.title: Uncertainty quantification in metric spaces
papers.abstract: This paper introduces a novel uncertainty quantification framework for regression models where the response takes values in a separable metric space, and the predictors are in a Euclidean space. The proposed algorithms can efficiently handle large datasets and are agnostic to the predictive base model used. Furthermore, the algorithms possess asymptotic consistency guarantees and, in some special homoscedastic cases, we provide non-asymptotic guarantees. To illustrate the effectiveness of the proposed uncertainty quantification framework, we use a linear regression model for metric responses (known as the global Fréchet model) in various clinical applications related to precision and digital medicine. The different clinical outcomes analyzed are represented as complex statistical objects, including multivariate Euclidean data, Laplacian graphs, and probability distributions.

llm.relevance_to_user: 该论文提出的度量空间不确定性量化框架可迁移至生物力学代理模型，但未涉及有限元仿真或植入物设计。

summary_zh.method: 提出与基模型无关的不确定性量化算法，适用于大规模数据集。
summary_zh.result: 在临床应用中展示了框架对复杂统计对象（如多元数据、图、分布）的有效性。
summary_zh.validation: 通过线性回归模型在数字医学数据集上验证，包括理论一致性和数值实验。

summary_en.motivation: To develop an efficient and theoretically grounded uncertainty quantification framework for regression models with metric-space responses.
summary_en.method: Proposes base-model-agnostic algorithms with asymptotic consistency guarantees, capable of handling large datasets.
summary_en.result: Demonstrates effectiveness on clinical applications involving complex statistical objects such as multivariate data, Laplacian graphs, and probability distributions.
summary_en.validation: Validated via the global Fréchet model on digital medicine datasets, with both asymptotic and non-asymptotic guarantees in homoscedastic cases.

papers.title: ATDM:An Anthropomorphic Aerial Tendon-driven Manipulator with Low-Inertia and High-Stiffness
papers.abstract: Aerial Manipulator Systems (AMS) have garnered significant interest for their utility in aerial operations. Nonetheless, challenges related to the manipulator's limited stiffness and the coupling disturbance with manipulator movement persist. This paper introduces the Aerial Tendon-Driven Manipulator (ATDM), an innovative AMS that integrates a hexrotor Unmanned Aerial Vehicle (UAV) with a 4-degree-of-freedom (4-DOF) anthropomorphic tendon-driven manipulator. The design of the manipulator is anatomically inspired, emulating the human arm anatomy from the shoulder joint downward. To enhance the structural integrity and performance, finite element topology optimization and lattice optimization are employed on the links to replicate the radially graded structure characteristic of bone, this approach effectively reduces weight and inertia while simultaneously maximizing stiffness. A novel tensioning mechanism with adjustable tension is introduced to address cable relaxation, and a Tension-amplification tendon mechanism is implemented to increase the manipulator's overall stiffness and output. The paper presents a kinematic model based on virtual coupled joints, a comprehensive workspace analysis, and detailed calculations of output torques and stiffness for individual arm joints.   The prototype arm has a total weight of 2.7 kg, with the end effector contributing only 0.818 kg. By positioning all actuators at the base, coupling disturbance are minimized. The paper includes a detailed mechanical design and validates the system's performance through semi-physical multi-body dynamics simulations, confirming the efficacy of the proposed design.

llm.relevance_to_user: 该论文涉及仿生梯度结构设计和拓扑优化，但应用于无人机机械臂而非生物医学植入物，且无LPBF制造或疲劳测试。
llm.why_not_core: No LPBF fabrication, no mechanical testing (fatigue or static), no osseointegration or surface roughness analysis, and no biomedical implant context.

summary_en.motivation: To enhance stiffness and reduce coupling disturbance in aerial manipulator systems.
summary_en.method: An anthropomorphic tendon-driven manipulator is designed with topology and lattice optimization inspired by bone's radially graded structure.
summary_en.result: The prototype arm weighs 2.7 kg with a low-inertia end effector, and semi-physical simulations confirm improved stiffness and reduced disturbance.

papers.title: Off-Road Autonomy Validation Using Scalable Digital Twin Simulations Within High-Performance Computing Clusters
papers.abstract: Off-road autonomy validation presents unique challenges due to the unpredictable and dynamic nature of off-road environments. Traditional methods focusing on sequentially sweeping across the parameter space for variability analysis struggle to comprehensively assess the performance and safety of off-road autonomous systems within the imposed time constraints. This paper proposes leveraging scalable digital twin simulations within high-performance computing (HPC) clusters to address this challenge. By harnessing the computational power of HPC clusters, our approach aims to provide a scalable and efficient means to validate off-road autonomy algorithms, enabling rapid iteration and testing of autonomy algorithms under various conditions. We demonstrate the effectiveness of our framework through performance evaluations of the HPC cluster in terms of simulation parallelization and present the systematic variability analysis of a candidate off-road autonomy algorithm to identify potential vulnerabilities in the autonomy stack's perception, planning and control modules.

llm.relevance_to_user: 该论文聚焦于越野自动驾驶的仿真验证，与生物打印中的AI应用无直接关联。
llm.why_not_core: This paper does not involve bioprinting, AI-driven bioprinting workflow, or any biomedical context.

summary_zh.result: 展示了仿真并行化性能，并系统分析了算法在感知、规划、控制模块的脆弱性。
summary_zh.validation: 通过HPC集群性能评估和算法变异性分析验证。

summary_en.motivation: Off-road autonomy validation is challenged by unpredictable environments and large parameter spaces.
summary_en.method: A scalable digital twin simulation framework on HPC clusters is proposed for parallelized testing.
summary_en.result: The framework demonstrates efficient simulation parallelization and identifies vulnerabilities in perception, planning, and control modules.
summary_en.validation: Validation is performed via HPC cluster performance evaluation and systematic variability analysis of the autonomy algorithm.
